newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian CLB says fraud covered in 1996 accounts.
newsitem.headline: Belgian CLB says fraud covered in 1996 accounts.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais Belgium (CLB), a unit of French banking group Credit Lyonnais, said on Monday costs linked to a major fraud against the bank discovered earlier this year had been absorbed fully in 1996 accounts.
"All the financial consequences of the...fraud have been incorporated in 1996 accounts," chief executive officer Phillipe Cloes told a news conference on 1996 earnings.
He said that the bank had used internal funds to provision for the fraud, but declined to give an exact figure. When asked whether the sum was a few hundred millions, he said, "not more than that."
Cloes said he was "110 percent" sure that the bank would fully recover any stolen money from the perpetrators, from any third parties involved in the fraud and through insurance cover.
He said three people left the bank including the head of its internal audit department in the wake of the discovery.
Earlier CLB had said the fraud would have no impact on future earnings.

"The bank had excellent commercial and financial health in 1996. This trend continued in the first months of 1997 despite the fact the bank was the victim of a large-scale fraud," it said in a statement.
The bank said in March a former employee had stolen 3.5 billion Belgian francs. The ex-employee and her husband have since been arrested.
Net profit jumped to 821 million Belgian francs in 1996 from 628 million in 1995. Profit was 383 million francs in the first quarter of 1997.
Cloes said he hoped the bank would earn 1997 net profit of more than one billion francs "if things continue as well as they do."
